fact: A Ministry of Digital Transition AI expert presented the national strategy for designing and deploying an AI model adapted to Burkinabe realities, on 12 August 2026.
The minister said the PACDIGITAL project, run by the Ministry of Digital Transition, provides substantial funding to set up AI centres of excellence and study grants.
Specialists at CITADEL, Virtual University of Burkina, developed a Mooré-to-French and French-to-Mooré translation tool, shown in a live demonstration on 21 October 2025.

On 15 October 2026 the Centre Citadel and the Data Lab launched L'Essentiel.bf in Ouagadougou, a free web and mobile platform that uses AI to collect, summarise and serve news from four national outlets every 15 minutes in French and Mooré, as text and audio (leFaso.net).

The government says its universities and research centres are studying over fifty AI solutions, including an automatic French-Mooré translation, transcription and speech platform and the LegiChat legal-text question app, with no release stated.

The minister told parliament that the digital transition ministry was finalising the DJAM AI engine for analysing threats to social cohesion in text and audio, and two chatbots, one on communications regulation and one on legislation built on LegiBurkina.

Burkina Faso plans AI models for Moore, Dioula and Fulfulde under its AI roadmap, and Dr Yaya Traore says agreements have been signed with the national broadcaster RTB to collect the language data needed.

Digital Magazine Burkina reports that AI agents developed by local structures were showcased at the 2026 forum of ministry IT directors opened on 26 October 2026, and that the ministry stresses local ownership of AI solutions.

fact: Agence Ecofin says a workshop at Koudougou on 24-28 March 2026, run by the digital ministry with RTB and CITADEL, worked on language formalisation and corpus building in Moore, Dioula, Fulfulde and Gulmancema for speech recognition, machine translation and speech synthesis tools.
